title: FPGA-Based Approximate Multiplier for FP8
problem: FP8 multiplication in neural networks incurs significant power consumption despite FP8's superior dynamic range compared to INT8. Existing FPGA-based 8-bit multiplier designs have high resource utilization.
motivation: Optimizing FP8 multiplication is critical for efficient neural network inference as FP8 adoption increases for deep learning workloads.
method: The authors analyze bit patterns in FP8 numbers to identify where approximations—skipping certain calculation steps—still produce results accurate enough for neural networks. They implement this approximate multiplier on AMD and Altera FPGAs using standard hardware building blocks and layout templates, optimized for minimal resource use. They verify the design through accuracy and resource measurements, then test it in actual neural network inference to confirm power efficiency.
key_novelty: This work creates the first FPGA-based multiplier that approximates FP8 math—trading perfect accuracy for faster, lower-power computation—establishing a benchmark for efficient low-precision floating-point arithmetic.
contributions: Bit-level analysis of FP8 approximation methods for multiplication
Fine-grained optimized FPGA implementation for AMD and Altera platforms using primitives and layout constraints
Achieves minimal LUT consumption compared to previous 8-bit FPGA designs
Demonstrates superior power efficiency in neural network inference
primary_theme: Low-precision floating-point arithmetic optimization on FPGAs
